correctness.rationale: For the specified fixed binary alphabet, greedily completed two-symbol arches both embed every shorter binary word and produce a specific absent word one symbol longer. The arithmetic paperfolding definition gives exactly four eight-position templates 110a100b. A complete two-state scan yields completed arches 2+b or 3+b and an outgoing state set by b, telescoping to U(8k)=3k+p(k-1)-1. All offsets 1..7 yield 3k+h_r(a), with h=(0,0,1,1,2-a,2,2). This proves the floor formula and both sharp discrepancy constants for all positive N; the included executable independently checks two generators, the full small transition table, 262143 prefixes, and brute universality up to length 28. Finite experiments alone are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Subsequence universality (equivalently shortest absent scattered-subsequence length minus one) is a standard natural invariant of finite strings, and evaluating it at every prefix of a canonical aperiodic automatic sequence is a motivated structural classification. Unlike ordinary linear-time input algorithms or a selected finite cutoff, the result provides an all-N closed form, an exact 3/8 rate, and sharp two-sided bounded fluctuations with infinite families of equality. It discriminates a deterministic low-complexity word by a completeness invariant and does not depend on unsupported applications or trivial parameter substitution.
